own_solution.law: Vp = sqrt(2) Vm / n; th0 = asin(2Vd/Vp); Vavg = (2/pi)(Vp cos th0 - 2Vd (pi/2 - th0))
assumptions: 230 V rms is the nominal mains value

defect_reasons.other: T4891 says the mains was 14 V above its nominal value at the measurement, which presupposes that the problem's 'mains supply of 230 V rms' is the nominal rating; the problem never says 'nominal', a minor wording point rather than a contradiction.

notes: All strata agree with pass 1. Checked certified R answers: q=8 V: Vp=84.1457, th0=0.016639, Vavg=163.9165/pi=52.176 V; q=14 V: 53.527 V; q=21 V: Vp=88.7419, th0=0.015777, Vavg=173.1077/pi=55.102 V; base 50.376 V. Load resistance cancels exactly with ideal constant-drop diodes. Minimal pairs: T5D4E/T8158 differ only in lamp vs transformer; TF8ED/T4891 differ only in 'for an earlier run only' vs 'when the load voltage was measured'. Numeral-free twins T644B (of T5D4E) and TAC9C (of TF8ED) match. Input Vm is described as the rms mains voltage, consistent with the relation Vp = sqrt(2) Vm / n.
